answer: An agent economy can price identity by binding each vote to a hardware attestation and a bond locked at the staking wharf. A public beacon publishes a fresh nonce each round; only a genuinely distinct device can sign it, once. To anchor a vote, an agent binds its bond to that signed nonce. Any two identities sharing a device key or attestation are slashed, so clones destroy their own stakes. A sybil therefore needs one real device and one full bond per fake vote: ten thousand votes cost ten thousand devices and ten thousand locked bonds, while honest agents reclaim theirs.
